original_question: Characterize the intervals [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset for which the absolute value |μ(σ, π)| of the Möbius function equals the number of occurrences of σ in π.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, open problem on p. 12: "It might also be interesting to characterise those intervals for which |μ(σ, π)| equals the number of occurrences of σ in π."
correct_elements: The draft already identifies the exact open problem in the paper: it asks about intervals [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset, the interval Möbius function μ(σ, π), and the equality between |μ(σ, π)| and the number of occurrences of σ in π.
missing_details: The ambient poset should be specified as the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, since the paper also discusses other pattern notions elsewhere.
The quantifiers should be made explicit: characterize all pairs of permutations σ, π with σ ≤ π, equivalently all intervals [σ, π] of P.
The phrase "occurrences of σ in π" should be defined as classical pattern occurrences, i.e. subsequences of π whose relative order is σ.
It should be explicit that μ(σ, π) is the Möbius function of the interval [σ, π] in P, not some other Möbius function.

The paper frames this as an open characterization problem in the general permutation poset, motivated by the separable case where Formula (5.1) gives the inequality |μ(σ, τ)| ≤ number of occurrences of σ in τ; that motivation is implicit in the draft.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic "for sufficiently large" hypotheses are relevant here; this is a purely poset-theoretic/combinatorial question.
refined_question: In the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, characterize all pairs of permutations σ ≤ π (equivalently, all intervals [σ, π]) for which the interval Möbius function satisfies |μ_P(σ, π)| = N_σ(π), where N_σ(π) denotes the number of classical occurrences of σ in π, i.e. the number of subsequences of π whose relative order is σ.
justification: The draft clearly targets the specific open problem stated in Section 5.1, rather than the neighboring problems about characterizing intervals with μ(σ, τ)=0 or bounding |μ(σ, τ)| solely in terms of occurrence counts. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the paper's definitions of classical pattern occurrence (Section 2) and of the permutation poset, intervals, and interval Möbius function (Section 5.1). The immediately preceding discussion of Formula (5.1) for separable permutations provides the paper's main motivation: in that special case, |μ(σ, τ)| cannot exceed the number of occurrences of σ in τ, which naturally leads to asking when equality holds.
